discrimination = treating people worse because of who they are
racism = the belief that some races are worse; unfair treatment based on race
prejudice = an unfair opinion formed without knowing the facts
stereotype = a too-simple idea about a group of people
tolerance = accepting people who are different from you
multicultural = including people from many cultures
human rights = basic rights that every person should have
freedom of speech = the right to say what you think, within the law
peace = a time without war
war = fighting between countries or groups with armies
army = the organisation of soldiers who fight on land
strike = when workers refuse to work to get better pay or conditions
demonstration = a public meeting or march to show you want change
petition = a document that many people sign to ask for change
slogan = a short phrase used to advertise an idea
banner = a long piece of cloth with a message on it
parliament = the group of people who make the laws of a country
prime minister = the head of government in some countries, including Poland and Britain
president = the head of state in some countries
member of parliament = a person elected to parliament
